candidates.name: Scleroderma
support_spans: ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin hardening, loss of skin elasticity, and hyperpigmentation are consistent with scleroderma, a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by thickening and hardening of the skin.

candidates.name: Scleredema
support_spans: stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks
contradict_spans: Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and hyperpigmentation could be consistent with scleredema, but the lack of inflammatory markers and normal laboratory tests make it less likely.

candidates.name: Lipodermatosclerosis
support_spans: subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin hardening and loss of skin elasticity, along with the histopathological findings of increased fibroblast density and adipocyte entrapment, could be consistent with lipodermatosclerosis, a condition characterized by scarring and hardening of the skin and subcutaneous tissue.
